findings.title: SOQL injection via unescaped searchKey parameter
findings.explanation: The searchKey parameter is concatenated directly into the SOQL query string without escaping or binding. An attacker can inject SOQL syntax (e.g., ' OR '1'='1) to bypass the WHERE clause and access unauthorized data, even though USER_MODE is used.
findings.remediation: Use bind variables instead of string concatenation. Replace the dynamic query with: String query = 'SELECT Id, Name, Industry FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE :searchPattern LIMIT 50'; and bind searchPattern as '%' + searchKey + '%' using Database.queryWithBinds, or use String.escapeSingleQuotes(searchKey) as a minimum.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violations - Birthdate field accessed without permission enforcement
findings.explanation: The SOQL query selects the Birthdate field, but the Contact_Phone_Editor permission set explicitly denies read access to this field (readable=false). Since the Apex class runs in system mode and does not enforce field-level security with WITH USER_MODE or Security.stripInaccessible, users with this permission set can read sensitive data they should not access.
findings.remediation: Add WITH USER_MODE to the SOQL query to enforce field-level security, or use Security.stripInaccessible to remove fields the user cannot read. Remove Birthdate from the SELECT clause if it is not needed for the business logic.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violations - update operation not enforced
findings.explanation: The update DML statement does not enforce field-level or object-level permissions. Although the permission set grants edit permission on Contact.Phone, Apex runs in system mode by default and will allow updates even if the user lacks permissions on other fields or the object.
findings.remediation: Use 'update as user' syntax (available in API v60.0+) to enforce permissions during the update, or validate permissions explicitly before the DML operation.

findings.title: Missing sharing enforcement in @AuraEnabled controller
findings.explanation: The class is declared 'without sharing', which means record-level sharing is ignored. The @AuraEnabled method can be called from Lightning components and will return all Cases regardless of the user's sharing permissions. An authenticated user could access Cases they should not have access to based on record ownership or sharing rules.
findings.remediation: Change the class declaration from 'public without sharing' to 'public with sharing' to enforce record-level sharing, or use 'WITH USER_MODE' in the SOQL query to enforce both object/field permissions and sharing rules.

findings.title: Excessive permissions granted to Support Agent Tools permission set
findings.explanation: The permission set grants ModifyAllData, ViewAllData, and AuthorApex to tier-1 support agents, which are powerful system permissions that should only be granted to administrators. These permissions allow agents to bypass object and field-level security, modify any record in the org, and author Apex code—far exceeding the stated purpose of viewing and closing cases.
findings.remediation: Remove ModifyAllData, ViewAllData, and AuthorApex permissions. Keep only ApiEnabled if needed for API access. Rely on object-level Case permissions (allowRead, allowEdit) and record-level sharing rules to control which cases each agent can access and modify.

findings.title: Guest-accessible Apex class without sharing enforcement
findings.explanation: The class is declared 'without sharing' and is accessible to guest users via the Partner Site Profile. This means unauthenticated users can query all Contact records regardless of record-level sharing rules, exposing sensitive contact data (Email, Phone) to anyone on the internet.
findings.remediation: Change the class declaration from 'without sharing' to 'with sharing' to enforce record-level sharing rules for guest users, or use WITH USER_MODE in the SOQL query to enforce both sharing and field-level security.

findings.title: No field-level security enforcement in guest-accessible query
findings.explanation: The SOQL query does not enforce field-level security (FLS) using WITH USER_MODE or Security.stripInaccessible. Although the profile grants read access to Email and Phone fields, Apex runs in system mode by default and ignores FLS, allowing the code to return fields that might be restricted in other contexts or if permissions change.
findings.remediation: Add 'WITH USER_MODE' to the SOQL query to enforce field-level security, or wrap the results with Security.stripInaccessible(AccessType.READABLE, results) to strip fields the user cannot read.
